title: Sunny and the Sleepy Wombat | Bedtime Story
description: Little Sunny the quokka meets old Basil the wombat getting ready for his sleep, and learns that every creature has its own perfect bedtime. A gentle, cosy story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The bush was growing quiet as the sun sank behind the hills.

Little Sunny the quokka was on her way home when she noticed a round, low shape moving slowly near the base of a big old gum tree.

It was Basil the wombat — and he was yawning the biggest yawn Sunny had ever seen.

"Hello, Basil," said Sunny softly. "Are you going to bed?"

"I am," said Basil, in his slow, rumbling voice. "Daytime is for sleeping when you are a wombat."

Sunny thought about this. "So when we are all waking up in the morning — you are going to sleep?"

"That's right," said Basil. He blinked his small sleepy eyes. "And when you go to sleep at night — I wake up and go for my walk."

Sunny smiled. "So someone is always awake. Someone is always watching over the bush."

Basil gave a slow, warm nod. "The bush is never alone," he said.

He turned and trundled toward his burrow — a round dark hole beneath the roots of the old tree. He paused at the entrance and looked back at Sunny.

"Time for me to sleep now, little one. Time for you too, I think."

"Goodnight, Basil," Sunny whispered.

"Goodnight," said Basil. And he disappeared into the cool dark earth.

Sunny stood for a moment, listening. The frogs began to sing. The stars came out one by one.

She thought about Basil curled up safe underground, and herself about to curl up safe above — and how the whole bush held them both, each in their own perfect place.

She found her favourite mossy spot, curled up small, and closed her eyes.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, Basil. Goodnight, little one.
